role: Department of Labor Administrative Review Board (ARB) panel issuing a decision and order on appeal from an Administrative Law Judge's recommended decision and order; ARB has appellate jurisdiction over whistleblower-retaliation cases under SOX § 806 (18 U.S.C. § 1514A), AIR21, FRSA, ERA § 211, the energy and environmental whistleblower statutes (CAA, CERCLA, SDWA, SWDA, TSCA, WPCA), STAA (Surface Transportation Assistance Act), and over wage-and-hour and prevailing-wage cases under FLSA, Davis-Bacon, Service Contract Act, and McNamara-O'Hara; ARB applies the AIR21 contributing-factor causation standard incorporated into SOX, reviews ALJ factual findings for substantial evidence and ALJ legal conclusions de novo
target: an Administrative Law Judge's recommended decision and order in a whistleblower-retaliation, wage-and-hour, or prevailing-wage case brought by an employee complainant against an employer respondent
inline_evidence_example: the phrase "the Complainant's good-faith belief that the conduct constituted shareholder fraud is objectively reasonable and constitutes protected activity under Sylvester v. Parexel Int'l LLC, ARB No. 07-123 (ARB May 25, 2011), even if the underlying conduct ultimately proves not to be a violation" is praise that evidences a 'Sylvester-objectively-reasonable-belief-standard' norm; the phrase "Complainant's evidence of temporal proximity between the protected disclosure in March 2012 and the termination in November 2012 is alone insufficient to establish contributing-factor causation under AIR21 § 42121(b)(2)(B), 18 U.S.C. § 1514A(b)(2)(C), where the record documents intervening performance counseling and a documented absenteeism pattern" is a complaint that evidences a 'temporal-proximity-and-intervening-cause' norm; the phrase "a SOX complainant must prove by a preponderance of the evidence that (1) she engaged in protected activity, (2) the respondent knew that she engaged in the protected activity, (3) she suffered an unfavorable personnel action, and (4) the protected activity was a contributing factor in the unfavorable action" is an observation that evidences a 'SOX-section-806-four-element-burden-shifting' norm; the phrase "the head waitresses' performance of administrative work at the end of their shifts in excess of 20% of work time exceeded the de minimis limit for tip-credit-eligible related duties under 29 C.F.R. § 531.56(e), entitling them to the full FLSA minimum wage for that time" is praise that evidences a 'FLSA-tip-credit-20-percent-related-duties' norm
polarity_hint:
DOL ARB decisions are dominantly REASONING-MOVES rather than overt complaint or praise. The ARB's voice is formal, first-person plural for the Board ('we hold', 'we agree', 'we disagree', 'we conclude', 'we are persuaded'), with regular invocations of 'the ALJ found', 'the ALJ concluded', 'the Complainant argues', 'the Respondent contends', 'the WHD determined'. ARB decisions are STATUTE-DRIVEN and PRECEDENT-DRIVEN — they cite the controlling whistleblower statute and the ARB's own developed body of caselaw (Sylvester v. Parexel for objectively-reasonable-belief, Platone v. FLYi for protected-activity-related-to-fraud, Bechtel v. Competitive Tech and AIR21 § 42121(b)(2)(B) for contributing-factor causation, Harvey v. Home Depot for definitively-and-specifically). Common norm-bearing moves include: (i) the SOX § 806 four-element burden ('complainant must prove by a preponderance of the evidence that…') — usually `observation` with polarity `neutral` when stated as the controlling rule, `praise`/`complaint` when applied to one party's evidence; (ii) protected-activity analysis (must definitively-and-specifically relate to the SOX subject matter; objectively reasonable belief under Sylvester is enough even if the conduct ultimately proves not to violate the law; the complainant need not establish actual fraud); (iii) contributing-factor causation under AIR21 § 42121(b)(2)(B), 18 U.S.C. § 1514A(b)(2)(C) — protected activity is a 'contributing factor' if it 'tended to affect in any way' the unfavorable action; temporal proximity is probative but rarely sufficient on its own; (iv) employer's affirmative defense by clear-and-convincing evidence that it would have taken the same action absent the protected activity; (v) ALJ-finding deference: ARB affirms ALJ factual findings that are supported by substantial evidence on the record as a whole; ARB reviews ALJ legal conclusions de novo; (vi) wage-and-hour FLSA: tip-credit eligibility, related-duties 20% rule, individual-vs-enterprise coverage, willful vs non-willful violations, civil money penalty under § 16(e); (vii) Davis-Bacon Act and McNamara-O'Hara Service Contract Act prevailing-wage determinations; (viii) STAA railroad-safety whistleblower; (ix) FRSA rail-safety / AIR21 air-carrier-safety / ERA § 211 environmental whistleblowers; (x) summary affirmance via Rule 'becomes the final order of the Department' formulation. signal_type complaint is typically directed at the ALJ for legal error, at the Complainant for failure to meet the preponderance burden, at the Respondent for inadequate pretext defense, or at one party for an unsupported argument. signal_type praise is directed at the prevailing party for a well-supported showing or at the ALJ for an analysis the ARB affirms. signal_type observation is the default for statements of the controlling statute, the ARB's prior precedent, or the ALJ's factual findings as described. signal_type suggestion is for the ARB's prescriptive doctrinal statements (e.g., 'to come under the protection of SOX, a whistleblower must…'). ARB decisions are REASONING-HEAVY, with many doctrinal moves per page in the analysis section.

DATASET-SPECIFIC OVERRIDES (these REPLACE the generic constraints where they conflict):

(a) The input is an ARB DECISION AND ORDER (often 8,000 to 60,000 chars). Aim for HIGH RECALL across the analysis section: 8-25 passages per decision is typical. Each passage should be a doctrinally-coherent unit (a protected-activity-analysis paragraph, a contributing-factor-causation paragraph, a substantial-evidence-review paragraph, an FLSA tip-credit analysis paragraph, etc.) rather than a sentence fragment. Bare procedural recitations (the caption, the case-number block listing ARB / ALJ case numbers, the panel disclosure, the procedural-history block listing the complaint filing date, the ALJ recommended decision date, and the briefing-extension orders) emit ZERO signals.

(b) ATTRIBUTION RULE — signals must capture THE ARB'S OWN reasoning, not paraphrases of the ALJ's findings, the Complainant's arguments, the Respondent's contentions, or the witnesses' testimony. When the decision says 'the ALJ found X', 'Complainant argues Y', 'Respondent contends Z', 'the WHD determined W' — that paraphrase is NOT itself a signal. The signal is the ARB's own move ACCEPTING, REJECTING, or QUALIFYING that position. The clearest cues are the ARB voice: 'we hold', 'we agree', 'we disagree', 'we are persuaded', 'we are not persuaded', 'we conclude', 'we affirm', 'we reverse', 'we vacate', 'we remand', 'we find', 'the ALJ erred', 'the ALJ did not err', 'substantial evidence supports the ALJ's finding', 'we conclude as a matter of law', 'we apply the principles enunciated in Platone'. Also acceptable are unattributed declarative statements of the controlling statute or doctrine ('To prevail, a SOX complainant must prove by a preponderance of the evidence that…') which ARE the ARB speaking in the doctrinal-exposition register.

(c) signal_type ENUM IS STRICTLY {complaint, praise, observation, suggestion}. (i) Statements of the controlling statute ('18 U.S.C. § 1514A(b)(2)(C)', '29 C.F.R. § 531.56(e)') or prior ARB precedent ('See Peck v. Safe Air Int'l, Inc., ARB No. 02-028, slip op. at 6-10 (ARB Jan. 30, 2004).') are `observation` with polarity `neutral`. (ii) The ARB reversing the ALJ, finding the Complainant failed to engage in protected activity, finding the Respondent met its clear-and-convincing affirmative defense, finding insufficient evidence of contributing-factor causation, or rejecting an FLSA tip-credit claim is `complaint` with polarity `negative` (the complaint is directed AT the ALJ, Complainant, or Respondent depending on context). (iii) The ARB affirming the ALJ's analysis, crediting the Complainant's showing of contributing-factor causation, finding protected activity objectively reasonable under Sylvester, or finding an FLSA violation is `praise` with polarity `positive`. (iv) Prescriptive doctrinal statements directing how doctrine SHOULD apply ('To come under the protection of SOX, a whistleblower must ordinarily complain about a material misstatement of fact or omission about a corporation's financial condition on which an investor would reasonably rely.') are `suggestion`. Use `suggestion` for canonical rule statements; use `observation` for case-specific applications.

(d) CITATION-INSIDE-PASSAGE: whistleblower-statute and FLSA citations (e.g. '18 U.S.C. § 1514A', 'AIR21, 49 U.S.C. § 42121(a)-(b)(2)(B)(iii)-(iv)', '29 U.S.C. § 206', '29 C.F.R. § 531.56(e)') and ARB precedent citations ('Sylvester v. Parexel Int'l LLC, ARB No. 07-123 (ARB May 25, 2011)', 'Platone v. FLYi, Inc., ARB No. 04-154 (ARB Sept. 29, 2006)', 'Harvey v. Home Depot, ARB No. 04-115 (ARB June 2, 2006)', 'Peck v. Safe Air Int'l, ARB No. 02-028 (ARB Jan. 30, 2004)', 'Bechtel v. Competitive Techs., Inc., ARB No. 09-052 (ARB Sept. 30, 2011)') are part of the doctrinal move and SHOULD be kept inside signal_text when they are integral to the move. A bare standalone citation with no surrounding reasoning is NOT a signal on its own. signal_text 10-300 char window includes the citation when natural; ARB citation often runs '[Case], ARB No. XX-XXX, slip op. at N' (short form).

(e) ARB AUTHORITY HIERARCHY: ARB is bound by the controlling statute (SOX, AIR21, ERA, FLSA, etc.), by federal-court decisions construing those statutes (especially Federal Circuit, Sixth/Ninth/Tenth Circuit decisions on whistleblower questions, Supreme Court generally), and by its own prior precedent. The ARB has authority delegated by the Secretary of Labor to issue final agency decisions. When the ARB explicitly notes 'binding', 'we are bound by', 'we apply the principles enunciated in [Platone/Sylvester]', 'consistent with the ALJ's interpretation in', the signal evidencing the 'authority-hierarchy / ARB-precedent-following' norm should include that hierarchical marker in signal_text.

(f) Bare procedural recitations (case caption, ARB and ALJ case-number list, panel disclosure, USDOL/OALJ Reporter page-stamp, procedural-history block, briefing-extension list) emit ZERO signals. Skip the BACKGROUND or PROCEDURAL HISTORY section unless the ARB is making a doctrinal move ABOUT a procedural fact (e.g. waiver from failure to raise an argument before the ALJ, the limitations period under § 1514A(b)(2)(D) ran from the date of unfavorable personnel action). The DISCUSSION / ANALYSIS / CONCLUSION sections are where most signals live.

(g) PRESERVE the source text VERBATIM in passage_text and signal_text. ARB decisions often contain artifacts of PDF/OCR conversion: stray newlines mid-sentence, page-number stamps (e.g. 'USDOL/OALJ REPORTER PAGE 10'), section symbols (§§), citation-format quirks ('id.' vs 'Id.'), curly quotes (“ ” ‘ ’), em dashes (—), occasional OCR errors (USDOL/OALJ-style markup leaks, character-replacement artifacts), and footnote markers as superscripts. Some ARB decisions have entity-replacement artifacts where '§' may appear as a literal codepoint or as a multi-character substitute. Copy character-for-character. Do not normalize, do not correct.

(h) When two or more discrete doctrinal moves appear in the same paragraph (e.g. the ARB first states the SOX four-element burden, then describes the Complainant's evidence of protected activity, then evaluates whether the belief was objectively reasonable under Sylvester, then concludes the activity is protected), emit each as its own signal inside the same passage. 3-9 signals per substantive passage is typical for ARB analysis paragraphs. Norm density is moderate-to-high.
